behavior: A diurnal hunter that watches from raised perches or hovers over open ground, then swoops or pounces on prey; it also catches insects and small vertebrates in flight. Flight combines rapid wingbeats with short glides, and perched birds often pump their tails. It nests in existing cavities rather than excavating its own.
field_marks: Two bold black vertical slashes on each side of the pale face
Small hooked dark bill, large dark eyes, and yellow-orange cere
Rusty back and tail with a dark band near the tail tip
Adult male has a slate-blue crown and wings; female has reddish-brown, dark-barred wings
Long pointed wings and a long, square-tipped tail
Yellow-orange legs and feet with dark talons
habitat: Open and semi-open landscapes with short vegetation, scattered trees or raised perches, and available nesting cavities, including grasslands, meadows, deserts, farmland, forest clearings, parks, and other developed areas.
